raw.body:
**Summary**

Since React 19.2, two documented behaviors interact to produce a transient window where
streamed Suspense content exists twice in the DOM:

1. **Batched/throttled Suspense reveals** (React 19.2 blog): when `$RC(...)` executes for a
   streamed segment, the reveal may be queued for ~300 ms instead of applying immediately.
2. **Client-rendering dehydrated boundaries on document load** (#31620): if the
   document finishes loading and hydration finds a Suspense boundary still "dehydrated
   pending", React client-renders it from the flight payload.

When both fire on the same boundary — reveal queued at t≈75 ms, document load + hydration at
t≈100 ms — the client render mounts a **visible** copy while the streamed segment
(`<div hidden id="S:0">…`) remains unconsumed in the DOM. Both copies coexist until the queued
reveal batch runs (~300 ms after `$RC`), finds the boundary already resolved, and deletes the
orphaned segments.

**Impact**

- End users: none observed — the extra copy is `hidden` (excluded from the accessibility
  tree) and self-cleans within ~300 ms.
- Tooling: any DOM-wide query during the window sees duplicates. Playwright strict-mode
  aborts immediately on the violation (no retry), producing persistent flaky failures for
  any assertion issued right after `page.goto()` to a streamed route. This bit us across
  ~27 spec files until we adopted `.filter({ visible: true })` everywhere (the mitigation
  the Next.js team recommends in vercel/next.js#86577 for the Activity/cacheComponents
  variant — which we do NOT use; our app has neither).

**Reproduction (deterministic, production build)**

Environment: Next.js 16.2.x (App Router), React 19.2.x, a route with `loading.tsx` whose RSC
payload streams after the shell (any data-bound page works).

1. `next build && next start`.
2. Warm the server (visit the route once) — a warm server makes hydration consistently win
   the race against the queued reveal. Cold servers rarely reproduce (hydration arrives after
   the reveal executed), which disguises the issue as a "flaky test under load".
3. Load the route with a `MutationObserver` installed at document-start; observe:
   - t≈62–77 ms: segments arrive into `<div hidden id="S:0">`; `$RC("B:0","S:0")` executes but
     the reveal is queued;
   - t≈103 ms: document load → hydration client-renders the pending boundary → second, visible
     copy appears;
   - t≈103–373 ms: both copies present (all test ids ×2; one copy under `[hidden]`);
   - t≈373 ms (300 ms after `$RC`): queued batch runs, orphaned segments are deleted.
4. Raw server HTML contains each node exactly once (verified via direct fetch) — the
   duplication is client-side; there is no hydration mismatch logged.

**Expected**

Either the queued reveal is cancelled/flushed synchronously when hydration decides to
client-render the boundary, or the client render consumes/removes the streamed segment
immediately — so the DOM never holds both copies.

**Notes**

- We could not find an existing issue describing this exact interaction (reveal batching ×
  document-load client render). Happy to provide the full MutationObserver traces and a
  minimal repo if useful.
- Related (different trigger, same symptom family): vercel/next.js#86577.
raw.title: Transient DOM duplication window (~300 ms) when batched Suspense reveal races hydration-time client render of dehydrated boundaries (React 19.2)
